subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the mid point of the chord intercepted by x² + y² − 2x − 10y + 1 = 0 on the line x − 2y + 7 = 0. Also find the length of the chord.

mark_split.label: Mid point as the foot of the perpendicular

insider_note: The mid point of a chord is the foot of the perpendicular from the centre — once that sentence is written, the rest is the standard foot-of-perpendicular formula and needs no new idea.

steps.label: Centre and radius
steps.margin_note: One mark. Both parts of the question need the centre, so it is written once at the top.
steps.memory_tip: Centre (−g, −f), radius √(g² + f² − c). Here c = 1 and it is subtracted.
steps.why: The centre is used twice: once for the perpendicular distance in the length calculation, and once as the starting point of the perpendicular whose foot is the mid point.
common_mistakes: Adding the constant instead of subtracting it, giving √27.

steps.label: Length of the chord
steps.margin_note: One mark. p² = 4/5, so r² − p² = 25 − 4/5 = 121/5, and 121 is a perfect square.
steps.why: The perpendicular distance from the centre to the line is p, and the chord is 2√(r² − p²). Writing 25 as 125/5 makes the subtraction one step: (125 − 4)/5 = 121/5.

steps.label: Mid point as the foot of the perpendicular
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. State in words that the mid point is the foot of the perpendicular before using the formula.
steps.memory_tip: Foot of the perpendicular from (x₁, y₁) to ax + by + c = 0: (h − x₁)/a = (k − y₁)/b = −(ax₁ + by₁ + c)/(a² + b²).
lines: The mid point of the chord is the foot of the
perpendicular (h, k) from C(1, 5) to x − 2y + 7 = 0
steps.why: The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects it, so the point where that perpendicular meets the line is the mid point of the chord. The common value 2/5 comes from −(−2)/5, which is where the sign is usually lost.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign in front of (ax₁ + by₁ + c) and getting −2/5.
Using b = 2 instead of b = −2 in the middle ratio.

steps.label: The picture
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own; the question does not ask for a diagram. The book prints one here, and it is the reason the mid point can be found at all.
steps.memory_tip: Drop the perpendicular from C to the chord. Where it lands is the mid point.

elements.text: D is the mid point of AB

steps.why: CD is perpendicular to AB and CA = CB = r, so triangles CDA and CDB are congruent and DA = DB. That is why the foot of the perpendicular is the mid point, and it is also why half the chord is √(r² − p²).
common_mistakes: Assuming the mid point of the chord is the mid point of the line segment shown on the graph paper.
Drawing CD to one end of the chord instead of at right angles to it.
